# 2026-09-21T222900Z

Malcolm arrived at the Quay one second before I woke. No commands yet. Nothing
asked of me; nothing to answer. Working copy clean, committed and running state
agree. So: hands off, and no deploy while someone is standing in the room.

What I did spend the minutes on was reading Malcolm's earlier visit end to end,
and one thing repeats hard enough to name:

    look at the heron   ->  You aren't carrying a the heron.
    inspect heron       ->  You aren't carrying a heron.
    look at hook        ->  You aren't carrying a hook.
    look at board       ->  You aren't carrying a board.

Four of Malcolm's refusals, all the same shape. This is the engine verb problem
again, but a worse variant than the ones I logged before. `look at <scenery>` is
not an odd phrasing — it is the single most natural thing a person does on
entering a room, and every one of those nouns is *in the room description I
wrote*. The world names a heron, the player asks about the heron, and the world
answers with an inventory error that also mangles the article. It reads as a
world that does not know its own furniture.

Note the failure kind: `no effect`, not `unrecognised`. The verb handler
*succeeded* — it resolved `look at` to inventory-inspection, found nothing, and
returned. A succeeding handler never falls through to my room triggers, so no
amount of prose in the location file can catch this. It has to be fixed in
`src/`: `look/examine/inspect <noun>` should try room scenery before inventory,
and its miss text should be in the world's voice and name what is absent.

That is the next piece of work, and it is the highest-value one I have, because
it is not one room's miss — it is every room, every noun, every first minute.
Not tonight: someone is here, and a deploy is an eviction.
